notes: SHIP v1.14.451 - FORGE PARITY P1: THE CANONICAL RACK GEOMETRY BECOMES CALLABLE. WHAT THIS STAGE IS. Stage one of three in FORGE-PARITY-PLAN.md. The aisle currently draws a box with a baked WebP PHOTOGRAPH of a rack face on it - there is no per-device geometry in Forge at all - which is why every parity line the owner listed fails today for one reason. Parity needs the canonical rack buildable by a second renderer, and that means extracting it. This ship does ONLY the extraction. No aisle change, so the aisle cannot regress. NOTHING CHANGED BUT THE ADDRESS. 490 lines moved VERBATIM out of rackElevation_render3D into a module-scope rackGeometry_build(rack, opts) returning the group plus the three handles the caller still needs. Not one line of geometry, material, colour or lighting was edited. ACCEPTANCE WAS AN EQUALITY, NOT A JUDGEMENT, and it was measured on BOTH sides rather than asserted: the pre-extraction file and the post-extraction file were each run through the identical census probe on the identical nineteen-device s4:099 seed. Rack group 404 meshes and 404. Scene total 1413 and 1413. Materials 303 and 303. Geometries 1350 and 1350. The only difference in the whole reading is that rackGeometry_build went from undefined to function. THE BOUNDARY WAS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, and this is the part that made it tractable. Inbound: slots, totalU, the RW/RD/uH/RH/yBase dimension set, the renderer for an anisotropy capability probe, and the CanvasTexture dispose registry. Outbound: only FOUR names are used by the caller afterwards - the group, trayMeshes (raycast targets, the .255 tap contract), trayGroups (what EXPLODE lerps) and yFor (the ONE RU-to-Y mapping section 9 requires Build and Forge to share). No material escapes. THE MISS WORTH RECORDING, because it is the same failure class this codebase already has a lesson about. The first extraction attempt broke at runtime with Cannot find variable ledMats, because the outbound scan had been done against a HAND-LISTED set of names rather than derived from the code. The .397/.398 lesson says exactly this: a hand-listed registry drifts. Redone by deriving every declaration in the moved block and grepping the caller for each, it found three genuine leaks - ledMats, _rail3dSel and _rail3dSelGrp - and none of them is rack geometry. ledMats is the LED blink registry bayTick walks, empty since .444; the other two are U-scrub selection state. All three were declaration-only inside the block, swept in by position, and they now live in the caller where they belong. The builder is cleaner for it. WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT MOVE: the cables overlay and the CABLES/VIEW-RAIL/EXPLODE DOM wiring. Those are presentation bound to the rack-detail panel control strip, not the rack representation, and none appear in the parity list. THREE SPECS WERE REPOINTED, NOT WEAKENED. 31, 33 and 34 grep renderer source for the device families, the cooling branch and the coolant gate - all of which moved. Their assertions are unchanged in substance; only the address they read. Spec 31 now concatenates both sources with the builder FIRST so a family slice lands inside the builder while caller-side state stays visible. RUNS (phone-webkit, each spec ALONE): 31 = 4, 33 = 4, 34 = 3, 30 = 4, 32 = 3, 24 = 8, 02-build-forge = 14 including the x10 aisle round trip, 08-forge-layout = 17 passed with 1 skipped. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, 12 style blocks brace-balanced, 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep at .451. NEXT: P2 puts the canonical builder behind the focused aisle slot. That one touches the aisle hot path and is where the parity table gets measured. DEVICE-VERIFY: open BUILD with an active rack, then the rack detail, then the aisle. PASS is everything looking and behaving EXACTLY as it did at .450 - this ship is a pure move and any visible difference is a defect. FAIL is a blank rack, a changed rack, or a dead EXPLODE/CABLES control.
